transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… I’m here because I’ve been blowing up at people, like over nothing. On operations calls I’ll just snap, and then I’m sitting there thinking, why did I say it like that? And it’s not just work—my family too. I mean, I’ve managed people for years, dealt with all kinds of problems, late shipments, staff issues, you know, all the usual chaos, and I’ve never been this kind of guy. It’s like my fuse is gone, and I don’t like what I’m doing.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if “down” is the word. It’s more like things just don’t land anymore. Like my wife will make dinner, and normally I’d be grateful, we’d talk a bit, kids going on about soccer practice and who scored or whatever… and I know I should feel happy sitting there. That’s my family, you know?

But it’s like there’s nothing in me that can answer back. I’m there, but I’m not really… feeling it. And then I start thinking about stupid things like whether I forgot to email someone back or if the garage door’s making that noise again, and meanwhile they’re all just being normal. I can see it, I know what I’m supposed to feel, but I just can’t seem to.
Do you find that you’re not getting pleasure out of things that used to make you happy, or that you feel down or hopeless most days?

Yeah… it’s more that I’m not getting anything out of things I know should make me happy. Like my wife will make dinner, or the kids are talking about soccer like they always do, and normally I’d be in it with them, you know? Asking who scored, joking around.

But lately I’m just sitting there. I know I should feel glad to be there with them, but it’s like there’s nothing in me that can respond. And then I start thinking about random stuff, like whether I paid some bill or if I need to call somebody back, and I’m missing the whole moment. So… yeah, I guess I’m not really feeling the good parts the way I used to.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the time?

I don’t know if I’d say depressed most of the time. I mean, I’m not walking around thinking, “Everything’s hopeless,” exactly. It’s more… flat, I guess.

Like this morning, I was making coffee and noticed the filter thing was bent—my wife bought this new kind because the old brand was out, and I remember thinking, why do they keep changing simple stuff? Then I’m standing there irritated about a coffee filter, and that’s the whole morning somehow. So… down? Maybe. But I’m not sure that’s the word I’d use.
Have you lost interest in activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy, like spending time with your family or anything else you used to look forward to?

Yeah… I mean, with my family especially. My wife will make dinner and the kids are talking about soccer, same as always, and I’m sitting there knowing I should feel glad to be there. I used to get pulled into it, ask questions, laugh at whatever they were arguing about.

But now it’s like… nothing in me really answers back. I’ll notice the food’s getting cold or one of the kids left their cleats by the door again, and then I’m thinking about that instead of actually being with them. So yeah, I guess I haven’t been looking forward to those moments the way I used to.
Do you often feel irritable or angry, even about small things, and does this happen frequently throughout the day?

Yeah. Yeah, that’s actually… that’s a big part of why I’m here.

I keep blowing up over stupid little things. Like on operations calls, somebody misses a detail or asks me something I feel like they should already know, and I just snap. And then five minutes later I’m thinking, why did I talk to them like that? That’s not how I’ve ever handled people.

And it’s not just work. At home too. My wife will ask me something normal, or the kids are making noise, and I’ll come back way too sharp. I mean, everybody gets irritated, sure, but this feels like it’s happening all day, over nothing. Like I’m already on edge before anybody even says anything.
Have you felt unusually tired or noticed a lack of energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

I’m not sure. I mean… tired, yeah, but I don’t know if it’s that kind of tired.

Some days I’ll sit down after work and realize I’ve been staring at the same email or the same spot on the wall for too long, but then I think, well, everybody’s tired, right? My wife says I look worn out, but she says that when I forget to shave too, so… I don’t know.

It’s not like I’ve been running marathons or anything. I just can’t really tell if it’s lack of energy or if I’m just… I don’t know, stuck.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or thinking clearly lately, like it's harder to make decisions or follow conversations?

Yeah… focusing, I guess that’s part of it. I mean, I’m not back at the plant — they still haven’t cleared me to go back in — so I’m trying to do what I can from home.

But even there, on calls, I’m missing stuff I shouldn’t miss. Somebody will be talking through an issue, and I’ll realize I didn’t catch the middle of it, or I’ll answer like I understood and then it turns out I missed the whole point. And then I get frustrated, and they get quiet, and… you know, it’s a whole thing.

I used to be the guy who kept everyone moving, kept track of the details. Now I’m sitting in my kitchen with my laptop open, and my neighbor’s dog is barking, or I notice the sink’s full of dishes, and suddenly I’m not even following what the team is saying. I’m worried I’m becoming a liability instead of the manager they need.
Have you found that nothing really gives you pleasure anymore, even things you used to really enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to say nothing ever, because that sounds dramatic, but… yeah, it’s like the normal stuff doesn’t land.

My wife will make dinner, or the kids are telling me about soccer or something funny from school, and I’m sitting there knowing I should feel glad. Like, this is my family, this is the part of the day I used to like. And it’s just… flat. Like there’s nothing in me that can answer back.

And then I start thinking about how my oldest needs new cleats, and whether I paid that bill, and whether the garage door is acting up again—sorry, that’s not what you asked. But yeah. The pleasure part… it feels like it’s just not there the way it used to be.
Have you found that you can’t enjoy anything at all anymore, even things you used to really like doing?

I mean… yeah, kind of. I don’t know if I’d say “anything at all,” because that sounds so final, but with the stuff that used to matter most, it’s like I’m not really there.

My wife will make dinner, or the kids will start talking about soccer like it’s just a normal night, and I know I’m supposed to feel glad. I used to like that noise, you know? Cleats by the door, someone asking where their water bottle is, my wife telling me the chicken’s getting cold… all of it.

But now I’m sitting there and it’s like there’s nothing in me that can answer back. I can see it should feel good, but it doesn’t reach me.
Have you found that you can’t feel any pleasure in things you used to really enjoy, like spending time with your family or other activities that mattered to you?

Yeah… that’s what I mean. Like with my family especially. My wife will make dinner, the kids are talking about soccer or what happened at practice, and it’s all the normal stuff I used to like being around.

And I know in my head I should feel happy to be sitting there with them. I’ll even think, come on, this is a good moment, pay attention. But it’s like there’s nothing in me that responds. It just sort of hits a wall.

And then I end up noticing something stupid, like a plate left on the counter or someone’s shin guards in the hallway, and I’m thinking about that instead of just… feeling glad to be there. So, yeah. I can tell those things should feel good, but they don’t really reach me.
Have you found that you can’t feel pleasure in almost anything anymore, even things you used to really enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s mostly the normal things that used to feel good. Like my wife will make dinner, and the kids are talking about soccer like it’s just another regular night, and I know I should feel glad to be there with them.

And I do know it, in my head. I’ll look around and think, this is what I’m supposed to want, right? Family, dinner, the kids being loud about practice or whatever. But it’s like… there’s nothing in me that can respond to it.

Then I start noticing dumb things, like whether someone left their bag in the hallway, or if I forgot to grab something from the store, and I’m not really in the moment anymore. But the main thing is, yeah… the pleasure just doesn’t seem to come through.
Have you found that you can’t feel pleasure in almost anything anymore, even things you used to really enjoy?

Yeah… I think I have. I mean, I keep coming back to the same kind of thing, but it’s the clearest example. My wife will make dinner, and the kids will be talking about soccer like everything is normal — practice, who scored, who forgot their cleats, all that — and I know I should feel glad to be sitting there with them.

And instead it’s like… nothing in me answers. I’m there, but I’m not really getting anything from it. Which is strange, because that used to be the kind of thing I liked, just the regular noise of the house.

Sorry, I know I’m repeating myself. It’s just hard to explain without sounding like I don’t care about them, because I do. It’s more like the feeling doesn’t come through.
Have you found that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, even ones you used to really enjoy?

Yeah… I guess that’s the best way to put it. It’s not like I’m choosing not to care, you know? Like my wife will make dinner and the kids are going on about soccer, and normally that would’ve been… I don’t know, the kind of regular family noise I liked.

And I’ll sit there thinking, this should feel good. I should feel lucky right now. But nothing really happens inside. It’s just flat.

Then I start noticing some random thing, like whether the table’s still sticky or somebody left their gear out, and I’m off thinking about that instead. But yeah… the interest or the good feeling, it just doesn’t seem to show up.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about being unable to feel pleasure or enjoyment in previously enjoyable things, which directly matches inability to experience positive emotions.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think I have. I mean, I keep coming back to the same kind of thing, but it’s the clearest example. My wife will make dinner, and the kids will be talking about soccer like everything is normal — practice, who scored, who forgot their cleats, all that — and I know I should feel glad to be sitting there with them.

And instead it’s like… nothing in me answers. I’m there, but I’m not really getting anything from it. Which is strange, because that used to be the kind of thing I liked, just the regular noise of the house.

Sorry, I know I’m repeating myself. It’s just hard to explain without sounding like I don’t care about them, because I do. It’s more like the feeling doesn’t come through.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest or pleasure in almost all activities, a key symptom distinguishing major depressive disorder from persistent depressive disorder or adjustment disorder with depressed mood.
doctor.question: Have you found that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, even ones you used to really enjoy?

target_item.name: Inability_Positive_Emotions
target_item.manifestation: My wife will make dinner or my kids will talk about soccer like normal, and I know I should feel glad to be there with them, but it’s like there’s nothing in me that can respond.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of pleasure or interest in activities that used to be enjoyable, which most directly matches inability to experience positive emotions.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I guess that’s the best way to put it. It’s not like I’m choosing not to care, you know? Like my wife will make dinner and the kids are going on about soccer, and normally that would’ve been… I don’t know, the kind of regular family noise I liked.

And I’ll sit there thinking, this should feel good. I should feel lucky right now. But nothing really happens inside. It’s just flat.

Then I start noticing some random thing, like whether the table’s still sticky or somebody left their gear out, and I’m off thinking about that instead. But yeah… the interest or the good feeling, it just doesn’t seem to show up.

inference.note: F43.22 (Adjustment disorder with depressed mood) is ruled out as symptoms appear more persistent and consistent with a major depressive episode rather than a reaction to a specific stressor. The presentation supports a unipolar depressive disorder, either recurrent or single episode, with irritability, anhedonia, and emotional flatness being prominent features.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a recurrent major depressive episode, moderate severity, characterized by persistent anhedonia, irritability, reduced interest in previously enjoyable activities, impaired concentration, and emotional flatness lasting for a duration consistent with recurrence. The symptoms are not better explained by a first-episode disorder, given the likely recurrence based on clinical presentation and the chronic nature of the current symptoms.
